lean.statement:
theorem result
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) :
    let phi : ℝ → ℝ := fun z => p.eval z
    ∃ hbase : MemLp phi 2 (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1),
      let b : ℝ := ‖hbase.toLp phi‖ + 1
      (0 < b) ∧
      ∃ hfeature : ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
        MemLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ) 2 (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E),
        ∀ w : {w : E // ‖w‖ = 1},
          ‖(hfeature w).toLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ)‖ = ‖hbase.toLp phi‖ ∧
          ‖(hfeature w).toLp (fun x : E => phi ⟪w.1, x⟫_ℝ)‖ ≤ b
approved_definition_context: ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E is the actual centered identity-covariance standard Gaussian on the stated finite-dimensional real inner-product space; gaussianReal 0 1 is the actual one-dimensional N(0,1) law.
Polynomial.eval is literal finite real polynomial evaluation, not an abstract random variable. Inner products use the displayed real Hilbert structure.
MemLp f 2 mu is actual L2 membership; h.toLp f is its genuine almost-everywhere class and its norm is the L2 norm under mu. Membership proofs are propositions, not choices of a different function.
